 "Whether the Taj Hotel Employees Association  has locus standi to raise this Industrial Dispute  and whether S/Shri Subhash Kant Jha and 36  Ors. (as given in Annexure A) are workmen  as defined under I.D. Act, 1947 and if so, whether  action of Management in retiring them at age of  55 years is illegal and/or unjustified; and if so, to  what relief are they entitled and what directions  are necessary in this respect?"
 Annexure 'A' contains names of 37 Claimants. 
2. One joint claim was filed against four respondents noted above. Separate written statements were filed by management no.1 and management no.2 to the joint claim. An application was filed by management no.4 for adopting written statement filed by management no.1 and management no.2, which was allowed. Vide order dated 14.10.2015, name of management no.3 was deleted from the array of parties. ID NO. 422/2019 Anil Kumar Banaik vs.
Taj Mahal Hotel & Ors.
3. Vide order dated 02.08.2018 passed by my Ld. Predecessor, the Claimants were directed to file their separate statement of claim, and the Ahlmad was directed to separate file of each individual Claimant and get those registered separately. 
4. The present matter pertains to Claimant Anil Kumar Banaik shown at S. No. 13 in Annexure-A of the reference.
5. It is stated in the claim that name of the Claimant appears in Annexure 'A' at S. No. 13. The Claimant was recruited by management no. 3 and as per requirement, placed in management no.1. 
He initially joined management no.1 Department w.e.f. 22.04.1981 as Assistant Steward. In November 1981, he was transferred from Management No.1 to Management No.2. He worked with management no. 2 Food and Beverages Department under the dictates and guidance of the officials of management no. 2. The Claimant was having no supervisory or managerial power. The Claimant worked sincerely and honestly and there was not an iota of allegation regarding his performance during his tenure. His services as Assistant Manager (Ticket No.- 1349) were forcibly discontinued w.e.f. 30.08.2013 at the age of ID NO. 422/2019 Anil Kumar Banaik vs. Taj Mahal Hotel & Ors. 55 years after completing around 34 years with it. His last drawn wages were Rs.28,999/-. The Taj Group of Hotels is a part of the Indian Hotels Co. Ltd (IHCL) under the management of TATA. The chain of Taj Group of Hotels spreads far and wide both within and outside India. The balance sheet of the hotels are prepared commonly by the IHCL. Therefore, all the units of IHCL should be treated and governed uniformly. Hence, so far as the employees of the IHCL are concerned, they should be treated at par in all respect. The retirement age of the ordinary employee on pay roll of the Indian Hotel Company in Delhi and Taj Bengal was 55 years whereas in Mumbai, it is 60 years. The Anil Kumar Banaik vs Taj Mahal Hotel And Ors on 24 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44417682/
2 difference in superannuation age is based on no reasonable classification. This difference is highly discriminatory and calls for a review. The retirement age under the brand name TATA should be uniformly 60 years and not 55 or 58 years. The difference of retirement age is highly discriminatory,
illegal and arbitrary. In fact, this is in violation of the fundamental right of equality of the employees of the IHCL and also amounts to unfair labour practice. Although age of superannuation is a matter of policy, the policy must be consistent and non-discriminatory. The management of IHCL,
therefore, ought to have examined this ID NO. 422/2019 Anil Kumar Banaik vs. Taj Mahal Hotel &
Ors. issue and must have taken steps towards removal of unjustified and illegal discrimination which amounts to unfair labour practice. Since the retirement age of employees in other companies under the brand name TATA is 60 years, there is no reason the same should not be adopted for the employee of IHCL uniformly. The retired employees of the respondents amalgamated and formed The Taj Hotel Employees Association registered with registration No.1510/2016. A legal notice dated 16.12.2013 was sent to the managements followed by legal notice of demand dated 10.02.2014 but no response was ever received. All the demands of the workman was ignored by the management despite numerous reminders. Conciliation proceedings initiated by the workman failed. During the course of the conciliation proceedings, the management enhanced the retirement age to 58 years effective from 20th January, 2015 and further to 60 years thus, excluding the workman from the benefits of the enhancement of age of retirement, which is not only illegal and arbitrary but also amounts to unfair labour practice and shows the flippant attitude of the managements towards their retired employees who devoted major part of their life working for the managements. All the employees who have ID NO. 422/2019 Anil Kumar Banaik vs. Taj Mahal Hotel & Ors. retired should be adequately compensated for the loss of years of service. Such employees are mentioned in the reference. 
6. The written statements filed by management no.1 and management no. 2 are more or less the same. As preliminary objections, it is submitted that the purported dispute as referred has not been properly espoused. The Taj Hotel Employees Associations is not a legal entity and has no locus standi to raise any dispute, much less any industrial dispute, or file any claim, against the management on behalf of the workmen employed by the Taj Mahal Hotel or Indian Hotels Company Ltd. The workmen employed with Taj Mahal Hotel or Indian Hotels Company Ltd are not members of the Association. The Claimant falls out of the ambit of definition of "Workman" in Section 2 (s) of the Industrial Disputes Act (hereinafter 'the Act'). Before his retirement, the Claimant Sh. Anil Banaik was working as Assistant Restaurant Manager with Taj Palace Hotel and his last drawn salary exceeded Rs. 10,000/- per month. In the capacity of Assistant Restaurant Manager, his main duties inter alia were as follows:
(a) Responsible for food and beverage service in the pre-determined area assigned to him;

(b) To conduct the functions of the F&B Manager in his absence;

(d) To originate and approve the general stores requisition, beverage requisition and the kitchen requisition as per par weekly/ daily schedules planned;
(e) To maintain stuff, stocks for silverware, china, linen, dry food stuff, stationary and non-alcoholic beverages.
(f) To recommend the periodic purchase of special items, both domestic and imported;
(g) To keep abreast with the competition by conducting periodic competition and market surveys;
(h) To conduct a menu engineering exercise annually to be able to identify the fast moving and slow moving items on the menu(s);
(i) To analyze guest comments and ensure that the negative factors in food quality and service were removed without causing further damage;
(j) To help in uniform inspections of service personnel and co-ordinate with the housekeeper for improvements, if any;
(k) To plan and conduct food festivals and promotions to up sell the slow moving and non-moving items on the menu(s);
(l) To ensure the timely pick-up and replenishment of all buffets;
(m) To ensure reasonable variety of daily buffets; ID NO. 422/2019 Anil Kumar Banaik vs. Taj Mahal Hotel & Ors.
(n) To liaise with the training manager to organize programmes for staff in the department;
(o) To make random checks and ensure that the quantities of various items indicated in the records were the same as the physical inventory;
(p) To ensure that pest control was done at regular intervals and regular schedules were maintained for the same;
(q) Responsible for maintaining reasonable cost control in the department without compromising on quality;
(r) To keep wastage of food to the minimum, by timely buffet replenishment, controlling food wastage, ensuring appropriate portions and checking pilferage;

4 (s) To account for the spoilage of food and beverage items and breakage of glassware and china;
(t) To maintain and enforce such systems and methods in the area of F&B service as laid down by the management;
(u) To develop new and superior methods of professional food and beverage service;
(v) To ensure proper accounting of all guest cheques and staff tips;
(w) To ensure that all banquet functions were conducted in a pre-planned manner, keeping the guests' requests in mind and also to ensure that such events would not disturb guests in other areas of the Hotel;
(x) To ensure that all room service orders were served within standard time, as per guest-request,
and with proper professional etiquette;

(y) To conduct daily briefings and ensure that shift beginning and shift and briefings were being held at the beginning and end of each shift;
(z) To ensure that employees in his department would conform to house rules and policies of the Hotel; (aa) To initiate the performance evaluation of his subordinate staff;
(ab) To formulate and ensure adherence to service standards;
(ac) To ensure the grooming of his subordinate staff as per the standards laid down by the management; (ad) To personally meet with ailing guests with special requests, and also to meet with any guest who had a complaint regarding food or a beverage or service provided by staff in his department and to resolve such complaints;
(ae) To ensure proper sanitation and safety in the operations of his department.
The services of the Claimant automatically came to an end on attaining the age of superannuation viz. 55 years. It is an admitted position that the age of superannuation of employees in the Taj Mahal Hotel, Delhi at the relevant time was 55 years. Hence, the Claimant had no right, much less any legal right, to continue in employment after attaining the age of superannuation. On this ground also, the Claimant does not fall in the definition of "Workman" under Section 2 (s) of the Act. ID NO.

He also applied for, and received, gratuity from the management on the basis that he had retired from service. The dispute raised by the Claimant is highly belated. On merits, it is submitted that the reference made in the claim to Hotel Taj Bengal and the hotels in Mumbai is irrelevant. Different units of the Indian Hotels Co. Ltd. have their own service conditions. In terms of a statutory Anil Kumar Banaik vs Taj Mahal Hotel And Ors on 24 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44417682/
5 settlement dated 20.01.2015 entered into by the management with the workmen concerned as represented by Taj Mahal Hotel Workers Union under the Industrial Disputes Act, w.e.f 20.01.2015,
the age of retirement/superannuation of the workmen of Taj Mahal Hotel who were on the rolls of the management on the said date, has been raised to 58 years. It was also agreed that the workmen who have already attained the age of superannuation and retired from service prior to the date of the settlement shall not be governed by the settlement nor they shall be entitled to raise any dispute or demand seeking enhanced age of retirement in terms of the settlement. The other contents of the claim are denied by the managements who have sought dismissal of the claim.

7. In his separate rejoinders to the WS of Management No. 1 and 2, the Claimant has controverted the pleas of the managements in the written statements and has reiterated those of his claim. 
8. From the pleadings of the parties, following issues were framed before separation of cases:-
1. Whether the claim of the workmen has been properly espoused by the Union? 
OPW 2. Whether the claim of the workmen is belated and suffers from latches, as alleged vide preliminary objection no.7 of the written statements of the managements? If so,
its effect? OPM 3. As per terms of reference. OPW 4. Relief. 
9. Although the claimant filed his affidavit as examination-in-chief, he did not tender the same nor appeared for his cross-examination. His evidence was closed by the order of the Tribunal. 
10. Since the affidavit filed as examination-in-chief by the Claimant was not tendered and in any case, the claimant did not appear for his cross-examination, there cannot be any doubt ID NO.
422/2019 Anil Kumar Banaik vs. Taj Mahal Hotel & Ors. that the affidavit cannot be read. The result is that there is no evidence led by the Claimant. 
11. Since the initial burden of proving his case was on the Claimant and no evidence was led by him,
the Managements were not called upon to lead their evidence. 
12. I have heard AR for the Claimant and have also gone through the record. 
13. My issue-wise findings are as follows:-
14. All the issues are being taken up together. Although at the time of framing of issues, the burden of proving issue no. 2 was put on the managements, there cannot be any doubt that the initial Anil Kumar Banaik vs Taj Mahal Hotel And Ors on 24 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44417682/
6 burden of proving his case was on the Claimant. 
15. As noted above, although the claimant filed his affidavit as examination-in-chief, he did not tender the same nor appeared for his cross-examination. Hence, there cannot be any doubt that the affidavit cannot be read. The result is that there is no evidence led by the Claimant. 
ID NO. 422/2019 Anil Kumar Banaik vs. Taj Mahal Hotel & Ors. 
16. Hence, there cannot be any doubt that the Claimant has failed to prove that his claim has been properly espoused by the union and that the Taj Mahal Employees Association has the locus standi to raise the present dispute and that the action of the management in retiring him at the age of 55 years is illegal and/or unjustified and that he is entitled to any relief. All the issues are, accordingly,
decided against the Claimant and the claim is dismissed. The reference in respect of claimant Anil Kumar Banaik is answered accordingly. 
17. A copy of the award be sent to GNCT of Delhi for publication. 
18. File be consigned to record room.

decided against the Claimant and the claim is dismissed.
The reference in respect of claimant Anil Kumar Banaik is answered accordingly.

18. File be consigned to record room.

illegal and arbitrary.
In fact, this is in violation of the fundamental right of equality of the employees of the IHCL and also amounts to unfair labour practice.
Although age of superannuation is a matter of policy, the policy must be consistent and non-discriminatory.
The management of IHCL,

Since the retirement age of employees in other companies under the brand name TATA is 60 years, there is no reason the same should not be adopted for the employee of IHCL uniformly.
